answer: Proof-of-stake acts as a fortress against Sybil actors by requiring capital commitment to validate network transitions. Rather than relying on an ivory tower of governance, the protocol forces participants to stake tokens, effectively pricing out fake nodes. If an attacker tries to spawn identities to harvest rewards, they must burn or lock significant timber-valued assets, turning their strategy into a barren orchard. The cost is high, ensuring that economic loss outweighs any potential gain from Sybil manipulation.
